findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the fail-quiet rationale to distinguish the two directions: OVER-broad owner sets (name-keyed functions, bare receivers) are fail-quiet (suppress firings), while unresolvable receivers are fail-loud (contribute nothing → the field fires and must be reported/markered).
evidence: Under owner-resolution a field is satisfied only if some read's resolved owner set contains its class; an unresolvable-receiver read yields an empty owner set and thus satisfies nothing, so if it is the field's only read the field FIRES
This is the primary source of the new firings the plan must enumerate and marker (the report+marker AC), i.e. it is the fail-LOUD direction, contradicting the stated 'suppresses a firing' framing
findings.finding: The plan's fail-quiet rationale mislabels the direction for unresolvable receivers: 'contribute nothing' means such a read satisfies no field, so a live field read only through an unresolvable receiver is newly FLAGGED (fail-loud), not suppressed.
findings.location: Design of the fix — 'Unresolvable receivers contribute nothing … an ambiguity suppresses a firing rather than inventing one.'
scenarios: A live field whose only read is via an unresolvable receiver (e.g. an unannotated param with no discoverable call site) is newly flagged and needs a marker — an implementer trusting the 'fail-quiet' framing may be surprised and mis-scope the newly-flagged list

findings.finding: The marker-accuracy AC requires a newly-flagged genuinely-inert field to cite 'a real open tracking ticket', but the plan does not state what to do if a newly-flagged inert field has NO existing tracking ticket — creating one is arguably the triage the scope forbids, leaving the executor without a default.

scenarios: The whole-schema re-run flags a field that is genuinely inert AND has no pre-existing tracking ticket; the executor cannot cite a reader, and opening a new tracking ticket edges into forbidden triage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence: 'If the whole-schema re-run flags an inert field with no existing tracking ticket, open a new tracking ticket capturing it (deferring the wire-or-delete decision to the operator) and cite that id in the marker — opening the tracker is not triage.'

The plan's own fail-quiet caveat concedes the ambiguity: 'Unresolvable receivers contribute nothing ... an ambiguity suppresses a firing rather than inventing one' — i.e. the bespoke resolver is a heuristic where a type checker would be authoritative
findings.finding: The plan designs a bespoke cross-module, flow-sensitive owner-resolution engine (parameter/variable annotation tracking, assignment propagation, return-annotation resolution, and a cross-module fixed point binding unannotated parameters from call sites) to answer 'which dataclass owns this attribute read', without considering established prior art — mypy is installed and already runs as a GATING full-src/rebar type check in this repo, and attribute-owner resolution is its core competency. No type checker (mypy/jedi/pyright/LibCST) is weighed or rejected, so the novelty of the hand-rolled inference is unjustified against the established approach already in the tree.
findings.location: Plan section 'Design of the fix' (steps 2-3), esp. 'a cross-module fixed point that binds unannotated PARAMETERS from their call sites'
scenarios: A field's only read is through a helper whose parameter is unannotated and reached via a call the fixed point cannot bind — the bespoke resolver stays silent (fail-quiet) and the field is falsely satisfied, exactly the ADR-0055/cc77 blind spot, whereas the repo could instead require the parameter be annotated (its existing remedy) and let mypy carry the resolution.
